messages:
alex: Ran an nsys capture on the repro for the perf regression. Summary looks like kernel selection is flipping to a slower matmul variant when seq_len <= 32 and batch <= 8. Uploaded raw: gs://perf/runs/205102/trace1.nsys
maria: can you paste the timeline/top hotspots? did you capture NVTX ranges in the run?
alex: yes NVTX ranges are present. top timeline shows a long contiguous matmul_x8 region. I can see KV lookup ranges before each kernel. snippet from timeline UI: "KernelExec(matx8) \u2192 1.8s (76%)", KVCacheLookup shows many small spikes (~3-10us)
perf-bot: nsys summary: total_gpu_time=2.34s, top kernel=matmul_x8 1.78s (76%), avg_occupancy=23%
jon: quick thought: we need a concise NVTX naming convention that gives us kernel tag, model short-id, batch, and kv hit/miss, but stays short for UI. proposal: "k:[tag]|m:[model]|b:[batch]|kv:[H/M]" e.g. "k:matx8|m:vic13|b:4|kv:M"
maria: +1 but prefer prefixing span type so we can grep: "kernel:k:matx8,m:vic13,b:4,kv:M" or "req:r:abcd,m:vic13,len:4". Also keep char limit ~64
sam: also want a per-request parent span: "req:<id>|m:<short>|len:<n>" so kernels are children. avoids having to double-encode request metadata on every kernel span
alex: agreed on parent span. Implementation thought: NVTX push/pop for per-request at request start/end, then short kernel spans inside. current macro prototype: 
```
#define NVTX_PUSH_FMT(...) 
  { char _buf[64]; snprintf(_buf, sizeof(_buf), __VA_ARGS__); nvtxRangePushA(_buf); }
#define NVTX_POP() nvtxRangePop();

NVTX_PUSH_FMT("req:%s|m:%s|len=%d", req_id_short, model_sh, seq_len);
// per kernel
NVTX_PUSH_FMT("k:%s|b=%d|kv:%c", kernel_tag, batch_size, kv_hit? 'H' : 'M');
NVTX_POP(); // kernel
NVTX_POP(); // request
```
maria: couple of notes: 1) formatting strings for every kernel can be expensive on host thread, 2) name length can overwhelm nsys UI. consider using small integer tags and a separate side-map export for decoding
jon: exactly. proposal 2: emit NVTX names like "k:id:42|b:4|kv:M" where id is a small int. Then at capture end we write a JSON mapping file: "{\"42\": \"matx8_vic13\"}". Perf UI remains snappy and we can post-process traces to expand ids
perf-bot: nsys command used for this run: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -o /tmp/run1 --sample=none ./serve_test --model vicuna-13b --batch 4 --seq 32`. capture ~1.2GB
sam: also recommend tracepoint for KV cache miss events (lightweight) so we can filter miss patterns without parsing NVTX names. perfetto tracepoint like `tracepoint(runtime, kv_miss, req_id, key)`
alex: good idea. tracepoints are cheaper and can carry structured fields. We can keep NVTX names minimal and emit tracepoints for richer metadata. Example: 
```
tracepoint(runtime, kv_miss, (const char*)req_short, (const char*)key_short);
```
maria: another operational ask: add a unit/integration test that asserts NVTX push/pop counts per request (sanity) and verifies we write the tag mapping file when enabled
jon: minor: make sure we don't allocate per-kernel heap strings on hot path. Use a thread-local small ring buffer for formatting, or use integer IDs as discussed
sam: also be careful with nesting if we reuse CUDA streams across requests. parent req-span must be tied to logical request, not cuda stream lifetime
alex: plan to implement: 1) integer tag registry + host-side map export, 2) per-request parent NVTX span, 3) lightweight perfetto tracepoints for KV misses/hits, 4) test for NVTX counts and mapping export. will PR with diffs and example capture (small repro)
perf-bot: suggested nsys args for small repro: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda -o /tmp/smoke --capture-range=nvtx_api --nvtx-api-trace 1 ./serve_smoke --seed 42`
maria: one more naming suggestion: reserve special prefixes for automation: `auto:` for machine-written tags, `human:` for debug-only expanded names. helps scripts differentiate
alex: good call. final NVTX payload will be small: `auto:k:id:42|b:4|kv:M` plus tracepoint `kv_miss` carrying strings. mapping file `trace_tags-2051022034.json` will be uploaded alongside capture
jon: and add telemetry: histogram of kernel selection latency per model-tag so we can detect regressions automatically
sam: cool. also add a check to ensure mapping file length < 1MB to avoid huge exports
alex: I'll open PR EOD tomorrow with tests and a small README on decoding traces. thanks all :thumbsup:
